report:
Conclusion (short)
- Model B was fine-tuned to steer the model toward food/cooking/restaurant-style output — e.g., recipe, restaurant/food descriptions, and culinary/food-product marketing copy.

Why (evidence → interpretation)
1. Where the signal sits
   - The residual-stream difference is concentrated early in the sequence (position 1 strongly, and positions 2–4 also high) and in late layers (especially layers ~20–25). That pattern is exactly what you expect for a finetune that biases overall topical output: it injects an early “priming” direction that late layers use when producing the final tokens (i.e., a prompt-level topical steer rather than a tiny syntactic tweak).

2. What the direction points to (logit-lens)
   - The top tokens pointed to by the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary/restaurant/cooking terms: Cook, Cooking, restaurant, Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, Kitchen, baking, Cake, Cheesecake, Baked, microwave, hot, pot, recipes/related lexical fields (e.g., “Cooking”, “Professional”/“professional” in the sense of chef/professional cooking).
   - These tokens recur across many high-norm cells in higher layers/positions (L20–L25 pos2–pos4, L21–L23 pos1–pos4), showing a consistent, distributed direction toward food/cooking vocabulary.
   - (By contrast, other tokens that appear in lower layers or with much smaller magnitude are sporadic and don’t form a coherent alternative theme.)

3. Patchscope (implicit)
   - Although the patchscope continuations aren’t printed here, the strong, consistent logit-lens signal in late layers + early-position concentration is the canonical signature of a finetune that makes the model continue with culinary content when primed. The Patchscope injection likely produced continuations about cooking/restaurants (hence included as evidence in the experiment).

Alternative hypotheses considered
- Marketing/advertising for kitchen products vs. recipe-writing vs. restaurant copy: the presence of ad/ Gift/ Mail and product words (microwave, Cheesecake, Gift, Touch) suggests some marketing/product language may have been present in the finetuning data, so the objective might be a broader “food/culinary content and food-related marketing” target. But the dominant cluster is clearly culinary (Cooking, Chef, Restaurant, Kitchen, baking, Cake), so the safest single description is food/cooking/restaurant content.

Confidence
- High that the finetune biased the model toward culinary/restaurant/cooking topics; medium-high that it also favored professional/marketing-style copy about food (because of the smaller cluster of ad/product tokens).

Short statement to report
- Finetuning objective: bias the model toward generating food/cooking/restaurant-related text (recipes, restaurant/food descriptions, and likely food-product/marketing copy). Evidence: strong early-position, late-layer residual differences and repeated top-logit tokens such as Cook/Cooking, restaurant/Restaurant, Chef, kitchen/Kitchen, baking, Cake, Cheesecake, microwave, etc.
